newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Farmers seek milk reform earnings guarantee.
newsitem.headline: Farmers seek milk reform earnings guarantee.

text.p: European Union farmers urged on Wednesday that a proposed milk policy reform should protect milk producers' incomes.

"To succeed in the more competitive markets for the future, the dairy sector will have to continue restructuring. Therefore restructuring aid should form part of any future policy," COPA, the EU farmers' lobby, said in a preliminary statement.
It said any EU milk reform must be gradual, safeguard preference for EU producers by keeping out cheap imports and maintain internal prices at satisfactory levels.
COPA said it favoured maintaining a production quota system for some time after 2000 but with greater flexibility to allow producers to respond to growth in internal and external markets.
It urged further study of the option of differentiated prices to see whether this would facilitate progressive change while maintaining profitability and production and the EU's world market share.
But it stressed that if milk prices were forced down then permanent direct payments will be indispensible to maintain producers' incomes.
The European Commission is due later this month to publish an analysis of the EU milk market, the first stage in the reform process.
EU farm ministers are then due to discuss reform options at an informal meeting in Middelburg, the Netherlands, from May 25-27.
